subject: Acme — Context-length & token-volume pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Evans <tom.evans@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme discovery — context-length & token volumes (follow-up)

Thanks again for taking time yesterday, Tom — great conversation. Quick recap of what we heard and next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of requirements:
- Primary use: contextual summarization + long-form QA over product docs and user transcripts.
- Expected concurrency: low-medium (5-20 concurrent users), intermittent spikes during end-of-day reports.
- Context-length needs: a mix — approx 60% of requests are <= 8k, 30% are 32k, and ~10% will need 128k for full-article/legal reviews.
- Average tokens (sample we discussed): avg prompt ~1,200 tokens, avg completion ~900 tokens (these are ballpark from your call).
- Monthly volumes (you mentioned): ~250M prompt tokens, ~350M completion tokens (monthly).

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Could you share the anonymized usage sample you mentioned (typical prompt + completion lengths over a week)? Attach to reply if convenient — that will let us produce an estimated unit cost.
2) Confirm whether the 128k requests are primarily batch/async (batching is ok) or interactive (low latency required).

What I can send next: a short pricing sketch (unit economics) and a recommended config (8k/32k/128k model splits, batching policy). I attached a short pricing sheet and example markup for a $/1M-token target to start the conversation.

Next steps:
- Tom: share the anonymized usage_sample.csv (sample format: timestamp, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, context_type).
- Marissa/Jordan: we’ll produce a 1-page cost estimate and an ops suggestion (KV caching + batching guidance) and propose times for a follow-up call.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_sheet_6-2027.pdf (pricing sketch), sample template (refer below).

Cheers,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

---
Redwood pricing sketch (high level) included in attachment: expected effective cost targets we commonly discuss: $400–$1,200 per 1M tokens depending on model family, quantization, and caching. For planning here I’ll produce a $/1M target assuming mixed 8k/32k/128k usage and batching improvements.

Thanks Marissa — attaching the anonymized sample for a 7-day period. Quick clarifications inline: 

- The 250M/350M numbers were our Q3 projections at the team level; for Q4 we expect ~x1.6 growth if adoption goes well.
- 128k use cases are 75% batch (ingest + async processing) and 25% interactive (legal review sessions). Interactive 128k requests are low frequency but need decent response time (sub-3s ideally).

Subject: Re: Acme discovery — context-length & token volumes (follow-up)

Appreciate the sample, Tom — that helps a lot. Quick initial cost sketch based on the sample and the split you described: 

Assumptions we used:
- Model family: mix of open LLMs (cost proxy used is Redwood-hosted open models); pricing bands below reflect model/quantization/ops.
- Batching & KV caching: we assume we can get ~18–25% effective token cost reduction across the dataset with prefix caching for repeat context (common in your support transcripts).
- 8k / 32k / 128k split: 60% / 30% / 10% respectively (per your call).

Estimated monthly token mix (from your provided week extrapolated):
- Prompt tokens: ~260M
- Completion tokens: ~360M
- Total tokens: ~620M

Unit economics (illustrative ranges):
- Baseline (no quant, interactive-optimized): $1,000 / 1M tokens
- With int8 / quantized kernels + batching: $650 / 1M tokens
- With dedicated reserved capacity (committed + caching): $420 / 1M tokens

Estimate for Acme (monthly):
- Conservative (baseline): $620k / month
- Optimized (quant + batching): ~$403k / month
- Committed reserved (annual discount + dedicated pool): ~$260k / month (requires commitment; we can model different terms)

Notes & tradeoffs:
- 128k interactive requests will inflate latency-sensitive costs; for those we recommend routing interactive 128k -> dedicated low-latency pool and batch the rest.
- If you can tolerate async for more of the 128k work, effective $/1M moves closer to the optimized band.

Next asks from us:
- Confirm whether you can commit a portion of 128k workloads to async (estimate what %).
- If you want, Jordan can put together a dedicated-capacity draft (throughput targets and pricing tiers) for your procurement team.

I’ve attached the detailed pricing sheet (redwood_pricing_sheet_6-2027.pdf) — it has worked examples and the math for the scenarios above. Would love to schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to walk through alternatives and the dedicated capacity model. Are you available Tue 22nd or Wed 23rd?

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_pricing_sheet_6-2027.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Jordan — forwarding the thread and the usage sample. TL;DR: Acme is high-potential: Q3 projected 250M/350M tokens, expects 60/30/10 8k/32k/128k split, 128k interactive is low-frequency but latency-sensitive. Prep requests: 

1) Can you run the attached CSV through our internal cost model and produce a 2-slide ops + cost breakdown? I want: expected $/1M under three configurations (hosted, quantized hosted, dedicated reserved).
2) Draft a suggested routing policy (latency tiers + fallback). Include assumptions (batch size, KV cache hit rate 15–25%).
3) If you can, mark any technical risks for interactive 128k (e.g., memory/latency limits) and recommended mitigations.

I’ll take point on the commercial side and sync with procurement. Prefer to have the internal packet ready by Mon 21st so we can hit a follow-up with Acme on Tue 22nd.

Thanks — Marissa
